title: CORS and Preflight: What, Why, How

scenes.line1: Why do browsers block some requests?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why your API call fails, even when the endpoint exists? Let's dig into CORS and preflight requests.

scenes.label: CORS
scenes.sub: Controls which domains can access your API.
scenes.say: CORS is what lets your server decide which websites can use its data. It's a browser security feature.
A preflight happens when your request uses a method other than GET or POST, sets custom headers, or uses a content type like JSON.

scenes.title: Preflight in Action
scenes.say: The browser sends an OPTIONS request first. The server replies with headers saying which domains and methods are allowed.

scenes.question: Do all POST requests skip preflight?
scenes.right: No—POST can trigger preflight if it uses custom headers or non-simple content types, like JSON.
scenes.say: Careful! Not every POST skips preflight. If you add custom headers or send JSON, the browser checks first.
